newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes chief rejects reorganisation offer - report.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes chief rejects reorganisation offer - report.

text.p: Mercedes-Benz AG chief executive Helmut Werner has rejected an offer to become deputy chairman of Daimler-Benz AG as part of a controversial restructuring, a German magazine said on Wednesday.

The magazine Wirtschafts Woche said Daimler chief executive Juergen Schrempp offered Werner the job of deputy at the industrial group and also that he would remain in charge of cars and trucks if he agreed to meld Mercedes within the group.
A summary of the article was distributed to the media in advance of publication. Daimler officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
According to press reports, Werner has resisted the reorganisation plan, demanding that Mercedes - the most profitable unit at Daimler - remain as an independent unit.
In an interview with Wirtschafts Woche, Schrempp said he hoped to reach a decision about the restructuring by year-end and have the plan implemented by the end of 1997.
"I am confident that by the end of the 1997 the new structure will be put into place," the magazine quoted Schrempp as saying.

Daimler, Germany's largest industrial group, is planning the reorganisation to speed up decision making and improve profitability and has previously said it will decide on the scheme on January 23, 1997.

One area of worry has been Mercedes' truck operation. But Schrempp said a new truck line launched earlier this autumn will reduce costs by about 500 million marks and that the division is looking to save another 500 million marks.
Schrempp said he was also optimistic that a buyer would be found for AEG-Electrocom, one of the remaining survivors of former Daimler unit AEG AG that has since been shut.

Daimler has also been considering ways to help its workforce feel more closely connected to the success of the company. Schrempp said the company was currently considering if it should make cash payments to workers when profits were better than average.
